Velocity structure and seismicity, catalog v5.1

Model v0.3.1, resolved nodes only. Catalog v5.1 with the v5.1 magnitudes, the v5.1 clustering and fault surfaces v1. 2026-11-25. Private working report; not peer reviewed. Code: workflow/06_analysis/v51_struct*.py on branch analysis/v51-struct.

Summary

  • Testable sample. 11.0% of the 168,406 located earthquakes (18,560) are in cells where Vp passes the checkerboard tests, and 2.9% (4,825) where Vp and Vs both pass, so Vp/Vs can be read. All of the Vp/Vs cells are at the Blanco transform, at the 15 and 18 km nodes (a few at 29 km). Vp alone is resolved in three places: the Blanco at 15, 18 and 29 km, the Gorda slab under Cape Mendocino at 29 km, and southwest Washington (Mount St. Helens, 1-9 km; Puget and the Cascades foothills, 15-18 km). The resolved volume holds about 53 independent checkerboard cells for Vp and 14 for Vp/Vs, summed over the resolved depth nodes. That cell count, not the number of events, limits every test below.
  • Q1, swarms against mainshock-aftershock sequences (Blanco only). 24 swarm and 34 mainshock-aftershock families have members in Vp/Vs-resolved cells. Their median Vp/Vs values are 1.727 and 1.729. The coverage-matched difference is -0.003 (95% block bootstrap [-0.042, +0.136], permutation p 0.93). The families fall in 11 blocks of 40 km, the swarms in 4, so a difference smaller than about 0.06 in Vp/Vs cannot be detected. Published differences between settings are 0.05-0.15. The data neither support nor exclude a fluid control of swarms.
  • Q2, where the events are. At the Blanco, the nodes that hold events are slower than coverage and depth predict. The event-weighted anomaly is -1.81% in Vp change ([-3.09, -0.23]) and -2.85% in Vs change ([-5.30, -0.06]). Randomized catalogs reach [-0.97, +0.94]% and [-1.23, +1.13]%, and the checkerboard inversion errors [-0.45, +0.24]% and [-1.21, +0.52]%. But the signal lives at the scale of single nodes (about 10 km), below the 40 km resolved cell. With the field smoothed to the resolved scale (Gaussian, sigma 20 km), the anomaly becomes -0.25% ([-0.89, +0.24]) for Vp and -1.02% ([-2.40, +0.61]) for Vs. Both intervals include zero. Under the rule that only resolved structure is interpreted, the Blanco result is not usable as structure. Vp/Vs at the events is not clearly higher (+0.025, [-0.014, +0.060]; smoothed +0.017, [-0.004, +0.032]). Nothing is found at the Mendocino triple junction or in Washington. b-value does not differ between slow and fast nodes in any zone.
  • Q3, depth extent. A Vp level cannot be tested: only 6 Blanco columns, and 0-3 elsewhere, have resolved Vp on both nodes around their 90th-percentile depth. Against the slab (Slab2, no tomography needed): in the Mendocino box the deepest well-located events lie a median 11.3 km below the slab top and do not follow its shape more closely than random pairing. In the Puget and onshore boxes they stop 27-31 km above the slab.
  • Q4, fault surfaces v1. 44 surfaces have at least 10 mesh vertices in Vp-resolved cells. Their normals are no more aligned with the horizontal Vp gradient than randomly rotated surfaces (mean alignment 0.70 against 0.66, p 0.15). They also do not sit at stronger gradients than other resolved nodes of the same coverage (median ratio 0.97, [0.79, 1.08]). At 40-60 km resolution a fault-scale contrast cannot be seen.
  • Q5, Blanco segments. The two western segments (West Blanco and Surveyor Depressions) have the highest Vp/Vs at their events (1.77 and 1.77) and the highest swarm shares (0.70, 0.66). The Blanco Ridge has the lowest Vp/Vs (1.70) and a swarm share of 0.41. Over five segments the Spearman correlation is 0.67 with exact p 0.27: a pattern to test with relocated swarms and a finer model, not a result.
  • Multiple tests. 77 tests are listed in tests_summary.csv. 12 have a Benjamini-Hochberg q below 0.05. Only those whose block-bootstrap interval also excludes the no-effect value count as passed. There are 8, all node-scale Blanco Q2 statistics: event-weighted coverage-matched Vp; event-weighted coverage-matched Vs; event-weighted coverage-matched dVp; event-weighted coverage-matched dVs; stratified Spearman(count, Vp_res); stratified Spearman(count, Vs_res); stratified Spearman(count, dVp_res); stratified Spearman(count, dVs_res). None passes at the resolved scale.

1. Data and selection

  • Catalog v5.1: 172,342 rows. Rows without a hypocentre (loc_source none) are left out of every spatial analysis: 623. Located: 171,719. Non-earthquakes (ComCat explosions, quarry blasts, other events; Texada quarry_blast_likely; is_earthquake False in the v5.1 magnitudes) are left out: 3,313. That leaves 168,406 located earthquakes.
  • Well-constrained depth (depth_good, the clusters piece's definition): tier A-C, depth_quality ok, not floor_limited, far_only or deep_pass: 98,204 events. Depth-sensitive variants use only these. Blanco depths outside the 2012-13 OBS deployment are depth_quality unconstrained, and the Blanco v5.1 depths are a median 2.9 km deeper than the Lange et al. (2026) OBS catalog (faults piece). Placement in the 15 or 18 km layer therefore depends on that bias.
  • Magnitudes: v5.1 M (mag piece). Mc per box from the clusters piece (v4 rule on v5.1 magnitudes). Clustering: the v5.1 nearest-neighbour families (types swarm, mainshock-aftershock, multiplet) and their classes. Fault surfaces v1: summary, assignment, and the 1 km mesh (constrained vertices only).
  • Model v0.3.1 (94 x 118 x 21 nodes, 0.125 x 0.1 deg, depth -3 to 125 km). Resolved Vp: resolution_p > 0. Resolved Vs: resolution_s > 0 and vs_reverted = 0. Vp/Vs needs both. These are the D-B018 checkerboard criteria (local correlation >= 0.7 and amplitude >= 0.5 at 40, 60 or 100 km cells, with pick noise, both pattern phases), merged under D-B049, and D-B051 for Vs. Resolved nodes: 888 for Vp, 279 for Vs, 224 for both. Resolved nodes in water or air by the v0.3.2 medium flag: 0. The D-B073 shallow-crust rule is not in v0.3.1 and is not used. Only the medium flag is read from v0.3.2.
  • An event belongs to the node nearest to its hypocentre (voxel boundaries halfway between nodes). A stricter variant requires all eight corners of the enclosing grid cell to be resolved: 6,383 events for Vp and 1,112 for Vp/Vs.

2. Method: controls for circularity

The events give the rays. Ray density (DWS) and resolution are therefore high where events are, and a tomographic error that follows the events would look like a structure-seismicity relation. Each test uses four controls:

  1. Coverage-matched anomaly. Each resolved node gets a stratum: zone x depth node x DWS tercile (P DWS for Vp, S DWS for Vs and Vp/Vs). V_res is the node value minus the mean over the resolved nodes of its stratum. A relation in V_res cannot come from depth or from the amount of ray coverage alone. DWS quintiles give the same results (t2_density.csv, columns *_q5).
  2. Randomized catalogs. The event set of each occupied node is moved to a random resolved node of the same stratum (2,000 times). This keeps the event clustering and the coverage. For Q1, family types are permuted among families of the same stratum.
  3. Block bootstrap. 95% intervals come from resampling 40 km blocks, the finest resolved checkerboard cell, with all events and nodes of a block together (2,000 resamples). Node-level permutations treat neighbouring nodes as independent when they are not, so the bootstrap interval is the one to use for the effect size.
  4. Synthetic inversion errors. The checkerboard inversions of each tile (40, 60 and 100 km cells; pick noise; pattern phases 0 and 1; and inversions started from perturbed hypocentres, noise_ploc) were run on the real event and station geometry. The error, recovered minus true, follows the events only through the inversion. The same statistics on these error fields give the size of an artefact.

Each event's catalog errors (horizontal sqrt((h_min^2 + h_max^2)/2)/1.515, vertical sig_z) are resampled 50 times to test the sensitivity to location. This only reassigns events to nodes; no hypocentre in any product is moved. Multiple tests: Benjamini-Hochberg q values over all tests (tests_summary.csv).

Swarm events are over-represented in Vp/Vs-resolved cells (7.4% against 2.9% overall). The Blanco swarms are what resolves the 15-18 km layer. Events on no fault surface are under-represented (0.4%). Nothing is resolved at Axial, Endeavour, Explorer or the Juan de Fuca ridge and plate, in Gorda above 29 km, or in the offshore Oregon and Washington forearc.

4. The Blanco at 15 and 18 km

Resolved nodes only: Vp change, Vs change and Vp/Vs at the 15 and 18 km nodes, with the events of each layer and the segment boundaries used in Q5.

Vp at these nodes is 7.1-8.4 km/s (5th-95th percentile; median 7.83), i.e. uppermost mantle velocities, and the Vp change from the start spans -10.9 to +5.2%. Vp/Vs at the 224 Vp/Vs-resolved nodes spans 1.62-1.88 (5th-95th percentile), with a median of 1.73. The starting model there is Kuna et al. (2019) 1-D, with Vp/Vs 1.73 in the mantle. Lange et al. (2026) report Vp/Vs above 2 in most of the fault zone, but higher up, in the crust; our model does not resolve the crust at the Blanco.

rho_depth_only: Spearman correlation between the event count of a node and the raw value, within zone x depth (coverage not matched). rho_cov: the same on the coverage-matched anomaly, averaged over strata. event_mean_res: the mean anomaly at the events. Units: % for changes, km/s for Vp and Vs, ratio for Vp/Vs. The table for well-constrained depths, events above Mc and background events only is in t2_density.csv. Their Blanco values have the same sign and size, e.g. depth_good Vp change -1.97% [-3.28, -0.37].

Reading. At the node scale, Blanco nodes with more events are slower in Vp and Vs at the same depth and coverage: -1.8% (Vp) and -2.9% (Vs). That is about 4 and 2 times the largest checkerboard artefact, and the inversions started from perturbed hypocentres do not give larger artefacts. It survives the location Monte Carlo at a smaller size (-1.34% and -1.95%) and DWS quintiles. It does not survive smoothing to the resolved scale (rows 'all, field smoothed 20 km' in t2_density.csv; open markers in the figure). The node-to-node spread of the Vp change at the Blanco is 4.9%, but only 1.2% after smoothing. Most of the variance, and the whole association with the events, sits at 10-20 km. The checkerboard tests (40, 60 and 100 km cells) do not certify that scale. Ten-kilometre structure there may be real (a damaged or hydrated transform mantle) or an inversion artefact that the checkerboard errors do not capture: those use true hypocentres and random noise, not the v5.1 Blanco depth bias. For the smoothed Vp/Vs and Vs, the randomized catalogs give p < 0.001 while the block bootstrap includes zero. A smoothed field is strongly autocorrelated, so the node permutation is too narrow there, and the bootstrap is the interval to read.

The Vp-level question is untestable on the resolved model. The checkerboards resolve isolated depth nodes (1-9, 15, 18 and 29 km, with gaps at 12, 21 and 25 km that the tomography notes attribute to the vertical checker pattern). Almost no column has resolved nodes on both sides of its seismicity bottom. The 6 Blanco columns do not show a common Vp at D90 (spread larger than for depths placed in other columns). For the slab: in the Mendocino box, D95 is below the slab top in almost every column, and D95 minus slab depth spreads as much as with randomly paired columns. In the Puget and onshore boxes, D95 is shallower where the slab is deeper (Spearman -0.49 and -0.62). Upper-plate seismicity there ends at a crustal depth, not at the slab.

Gradients are central differences between resolved nodes only (about 10-11 km apart). The model resolves 40-60 km cells, so it can show only whether a surface runs along a long-wavelength velocity boundary. Neither the absolute Vp (which includes the starting model's lateral structure) nor the Vp change shows alignment. Orientation is used for all surfaces, but the faults verifier found that 93 of the 142 surfaces change strike between detection reruns (median range 103 deg). The 'stable' rows, 10 surfaces for Vp, are the only ones whose orientation can be trusted. Their alignment is 0.78 against 0.68 (p 0.04; q 0.23 after the correction for multiple tests), on 10 surfaces in 7 blocks.

11. v4-era counterpart

The earlier analysis, phase13_tomography.py (Route A era, 09-29), compared an earlier catalog with external Vs models (Delph et al. 2018; CRESCENT CVM Gen0). It used dlnVs relative to each model's depth mean and no resolution mask or coverage control. No v4 structure-seismicity analysis exists on our own tomography: v0.3.1 did not exist before v5.1. The relocation moves Blanco events into faster CRESCENT Vs (+4.4 points in median dlnVs) because they moved deeper (median 9.3 to 15.6 km). In the other regions the median changes by -1.5 to +0.8 points (CRESCENT) and -0.5 to +2.7 points (Delph). These numbers mostly follow depth and geography. The external models are not affected by the circularity of our own tomography, but they have no resolution information at the event scale either. At the 1,993 Vp/Vs-resolved v5.1 events inside CRESCENT, its dlnVs and our coverage-matched Vs change correlate weakly (Spearman 0.16). CRESCENT Gen0 Vs is part of our starting model onshore (D-B005); at the Blanco the start is Kuna et al. (2019).

13. Proposed decisions

  1. Resolved means resolution_p > 0 for Vp, resolution_s > 0 and vs_reverted == 0 for Vs, and both for Vp/Vs, on v0.3.1 as published. The 12/21/25 km mask gaps are not bridged, and no DWS-only or tile-weight criterion is added.
  2. Events are sampled at the nearest node (voxel). The all-eight-corners rule is reported as a stricter count, not used for the tests.
  3. Circularity control: coverage-matched anomalies within zone x depth node x DWS tercile (P DWS for Vp, S DWS for Vs and Vp/Vs); randomized catalogs that move each node's event set to a random node of the same stratum; family types permuted within strata; 40 km block bootstrap (finest resolved checkerboard cell) for all intervals.
  4. Use the tiles' checkerboard inversion errors (recovered minus true, noise and noise_ploc, both pattern phases) as the artefact yardstick, interpolated from the tile lattices onto the merged grid.
  5. Event set: located earthquakes only (no loc_source none, no is_earthquake False). Depth-sensitive variants use depth_good (tier A-C, depth_quality ok, not floor_limited, far_only or deep_pass), the clusters piece's definition.
  6. Q1 family value: median over members in resolved cells, families with >= 3 such members; >= 50% (strict) and depth_good variants are reported.
  7. b-value: Aki-Utsu on M minus the Mc of the event's cluster box, events split at a coverage-matched anomaly of 0. Report only within a zone (D-B041).
  8. Blanco segments as longitude boxes (lat 42.4-45.0): WBD < -129.45 < SD < -128.95 < CD < -128.5 < BR < -127.45 < GD < -126.4, matching the v1 surfaces' literature names.
  9. Q3 depth extent: columns of one model node (0.125 x 0.1 deg) with >= 30 well-constrained events; Vp at D90/D95 only between two adjacent resolved depth nodes.
  10. Q4: constrained mesh vertices only; alignment of the horizontal normal with the horizontal gradient against random strike rotations; orientation results read only for the faults piece's 'stable' surfaces.
  11. Multiple testing: Benjamini-Hochberg over all tests in tests_summary.csv; report q with p.
  12. Test every relation also on the field smoothed to the resolved scale (Gaussian, sigma 20 km = half the finest resolved checkerboard cell); a relation that exists only at the node scale is reported as unresolved.
  13. Do not use this analysis for interpretation in the paper beyond the statement of what is untestable and the null results at the resolved scale, until the D-B077 re-inversion (v0.4.0) with its resolution tests (including a 20 km checkerboard or spike test at the Blanco) and its ensemble exists.

14. Open issues and limits

  • The resolved volume is small: about 53 independent Vp cells and 14 Vp/Vs cells. The D-B049 gate keeps the s480 tiles at full weight, but their checkerboards barely recover, so Gorda, Oregon and Washington are largely unresolved. Any structure-seismicity claim outside the Blanco needs a less smoothed or re-inverted model (D-B077) with new resolution tests.
  • The checkerboard masks are empty at 12, 21 and 25 km while neighbouring depths are resolved (tomography notes: probably the vertical checker sign changes). If the masks change, rerun every step.
  • The Blanco low-Vp/low-Vs association at the events exists only at the node scale (10-20 km), below the 40 km resolved cell, so the resolution tests do not cover it. It could be real or could come from a systematic trade-off with the v5.1 Blanco depth bias (+2.9 km median against Lange 2026); the checkerboards use true hypocentres plus random perturbations, not a systematic depth error. A 20 km checkerboard or spike test and a synthetic test with a systematic depth offset, on the D-B077 model, would settle it.
  • Vp/Vs at the Blanco (1.62-1.88 at resolved nodes) is close to the Kuna (2019) starting value of 1.73 in the mantle. Vs is reverted at most S-poor nodes (D-B051), so the Vp/Vs signal is weak by construction.
  • Family labels at the Blanco are partly reproduced by time-shuffled catalogs (39% of links, clusters verifier). Q1 inherits that uncertainty.
  • The fault surfaces used are the faults piece's committed v1 (6be76cfd). The verifier asked for relabelled Axial events and new flags (no effect here, because Axial has no resolved node) and for detection-level uncertainty: only stable surfaces should carry orientation results.
  • No ensemble posterior (D-B030/D-B032) exists for v0.3.1, so the velocity uncertainty at a node is not in the intervals; the block bootstrap covers spatial sampling only.
